title: ex fox legal head dinh joins law firm sullivan cromwell 2026 09 08
text:
Sept 8 (Reuters) - Former top Fox Corp (FOXA.O)
, opens new tab
 lawyer Viet Dinh is joining Sullivan & Cromwell, the Wall Street law firm said on Tuesday, three years after Dinh departed Fox in the wake of ​its $787.5 million settlement with Dominion Voting Systems.
Sullivan & Cromwell co-chairs Robert Giuffra and Scott Miller ‌said in a statement that Dinh would assist the firm's clients in their "most consequential strategic, transactional and crisis-management matters.”
Dinh was the chief legal and policy officer at Fox and part of its senior management team when it agreed in ​April 2023 to settle Dominion's claims that it was defamed by false vote-rigging claims that were aired ​by the news outlet known for its roster of conservative commentators. Dinh left Fox ⁠at the end of 2023 but continued to advise its leadership, Sullivan & Cromwell said. He will be ​a partner in the firm's Los Angeles office.
In a statement released by Sullivan & Cromwell, Dinh said he ​looked forward to working on "transformational transactions and bet-the-company litigations and investigations for our clients.”
Dinh was a former U.S. attorney general under President George W Bush and an architect of the Patriot Act, the U.S. national security law enacted after ​the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.
He was a founding partner of the Washington, D.C.-based litigation firm Bancroft ​PLLC, known for work on behalf of right-wing political causes, and was a partner at Kirkland & Ellis after it ‌absorbed Bancroft ⁠in 2016.
Dinh joined Fox in 2018. He received a lump-sum cash payment of $23 million as part of his separation agreement with the company. Since leaving the company, he became a principal at Palanquin Advisors, a venture capital firm, and sits on the board of directors of GrubHub parent Wonder and Irish ​building materials maker Kingspan ​Group, according to his ⁠LinkedIn profile.
A Sullivan & Cromwell spokesperson said Dinh will wind down Palanquin Advisors and transition his clients to the firm.
Lawyers at Sullivan & Cromwell are defending Republican ​President Donald Trump against charges that he falsified business records to cover up ​a $130,000 payment ⁠his former personal lawyer made to adult film actor Stormy Daniels for her silence before the 2016 presidential election about a sexual encounter she said she had with Trump years earlier. Trump has appealed his May 2024 ⁠conviction.
The ​firm is also representing Trump in his appeal to the New ​York Court of Appeals in the civil fraud case brought by Democratic New York Attorney General Letitia James. A state appeals court ​last year preserved the case while tossing a half-billion-dollar penalty a judge had entered.
